title: Neon Paddle Duel
description: Neon Paddle Duel is an original arcade game about two glowing paddles dueling under neon light. You guard the left wall while the ball ricochets around a dark court, and every clean return adds to your score. The court is small and fast, so rallies feel tense even when the paddle barely moves.
body:
Neon Paddle Duel is an original arcade game about two glowing paddles dueling under neon light. You guard the left wall while the ball ricochets around a dark court, and every clean return adds to your score. The court is small and fast, so rallies feel tense even when the paddle barely moves.

The rules are simple: move the paddle up, down, or hold it still each tick, and meet the ball when it reaches your wall. A return scores a point for you; a ball that slips past scores for the other side and resets the rally. The first player to build a commanding lead wins the duel, and the demo plays one scripted rally to show the rhythm.

The best tactic is the quiet paddle. Start low, drift toward the middle, and make your final move only when the ball is two steps from the wall. Players who chase every bounce overshoot; players who wait for the last moment meet the ball exactly where it arrives.
controls: Type up/down/stay each tick to guard your wall, quit to stop.

title: Lantern Maze Run
description: Lantern Maze Run is an original maze game set in a festival of paper lanterns. You guide a runner through lantern-lit lanes, gathering every lantern glow while a night watchman patrols the far side of the maze. The lanes twist around garden walls, and the watchman always walks toward your light, so every route is a choice between a shortcut and safety.
body:
Lantern Maze Run is an original maze game set in a festival of paper lanterns. You guide a runner through lantern-lit lanes, gathering every lantern glow while a night watchman patrols the far side of the maze. The lanes twist around garden walls, and the watchman always walks toward your light, so every route is a choice between a shortcut and safety.

The rules are straightforward: move up, down, left, or right, and each lantern glow you step on adds ten points. You have three lives, and meeting the watchman costs one and sends you back to the start of the maze. Clearing every glow wins the run; losing all three lives ends it.

Smart runners clear the near lanes first and save the far corner for last, when the watchman's patrol is predictable. Never enter a dead-end lane while the watchman is close, and always leave yourself a second way out. The maze rewards patience more than speed, and the best runs look almost lazy.
controls: Type up/down/left/right to move, quit to stop.

title: Starfall Defense
description: Starfall Defense is an original fixed shooter about holding a hillside observatory against falling star fragments. Rows of fragments drift down from the night sky, and your single ground cannon slides along the ridge to blast them before they land. Each fragment you destroy earns points, and the sky grows emptier and calmer with every clean column you clear.
body:
Starfall Defense is an original fixed shooter about holding a hillside observatory against falling star fragments. Rows of fragments drift down from the night sky, and your single ground cannon slides along the ridge to blast them before they land. Each fragment you destroy earns points, and the sky grows emptier and calmer with every clean column you clear.

The rules are simple: move left or right, fire upward, and clear every fragment before it reaches the ground line. A shot destroys the lowest fragment in your column, so working one column at a time is the fastest way to thin the sky. The demo plays a near-complete defense with one fragment left standing.

Column discipline wins this game. Finish a column before switching to the next, because a forgotten fragment in an old column is the one that lands while you are busy elsewhere. Move between shots, never during them, and the observatory will still be standing when the sky clears.
controls: Type left/right/shoot to move and fire, quit to stop.

title: Crystal Vector Drift
description: Crystal Vector Drift is an original vector-flight game about a small survey ship threading a field of floating crystals. The crystals hang in the dark like glass, and your ship's beam can shatter them, but every shattered crystal leaves smaller shards that drift on. The ship itself drifts with real momentum, so every thrust is a commitment.
body:
Crystal Vector Drift is an original vector-flight game about a small survey ship threading a field of floating crystals. The crystals hang in the dark like glass, and your ship's beam can shatter them, but every shattered crystal leaves smaller shards that drift on. The ship itself drifts with real momentum, so every thrust is a commitment.

The rules are clean: turn left or right, thrust to move two steps in the direction you face, and shoot to break crystals up to three steps ahead. Large crystals split into two smaller ones when hit, and small ones vanish for points. You have three lives, and touching a crystal costs one.

Drift pilots shoot from range and never chase a shard. Line up on a crystal row, fire until it breaks, and thrust clear before the shards settle. The pilots who last longest fire in short bursts and treat the ship's momentum as a glide, not a race.

title: Rooftop Runner
description: Rooftop Runner is an original platform game about a courier sprinting across city rooftops at dawn. Chimneys, gaps, and vents block the route, and the courier must jump each one or stumble and lose a life. The run is a single sprint from the first rooftop to the last, and the city skyline scrolls past as the courier keeps moving.
body:
Rooftop Runner is an original platform game about a courier sprinting across city rooftops at dawn. Chimneys, gaps, and vents block the route, and the courier must jump each one or stumble and lose a life. The run is a single sprint from the first rooftop to the last, and the city skyline scrolls past as the courier keeps moving.

The rules are simple: each tick you run or jump, and a jump carries you over two steps, so jumping just before an obstacle clears it cleanly. Running into an obstacle costs a life, but the run continues, and reaching the final rooftop wins the game. The demo plays a clean run with all three lives intact.

Jump early, not late. A jump started one step before the obstacle covers both the step you are on and the obstacle itself, while a jump started on the obstacle is already too late. Couriers who found the rhythm stopped thinking about jumping and simply felt the rooftops under their feet.
controls: Type jump/run each tick to clear obstacles, quit to stop.

title: Iron Fist Showdown
description: Iron Fist Showdown is an original versus fighting game about two martial artists meeting in a night tournament. Each fighter has a jab, a hook, a kick, a powerful special move, and a block, and the bout is a contest of reading the opponent rather than throwing the most punches. The crowd stays quiet between rounds and roars when a special lands.
body:
Iron Fist Showdown is an original versus fighting game about two martial artists meeting in a night tournament. Each fighter has a jab, a hook, a kick, a powerful special move, and a block, and the bout is a contest of reading the opponent rather than throwing the most punches. The crowd stays quiet between rounds and roars when a special lands.

The rules are direct: each round you choose a move and the computer answers with its own pattern of moves. Blocking cuts incoming damage to less than a third, and the special move needs several rounds to recharge after use. The fighter whose health reaches zero first loses, and a bout that ends with both standing is a draw.

The winning approach is patience with bursts. Block through the opponent's aggressive rounds, strike when they fall into a blocking habit, and save the special for a round when the opponent is not guarding. Fighters who threw specials on cooldown wasted them; fighters who waited landed them cleanly.
controls: Type jab/hook/kick/special/block each round, quit to stop.

title: Sunset Speedway
description: Sunset Speedway is an original racing game about a coastal sprint at dusk, where the road runs beside the sea and the light turns everything gold. You drive a small open-top car against three rivals, accelerating down straight stretches and choosing lanes around road hazards. The race is short, fast, and decided by clean driving.
body:
Sunset Speedway is an original racing game about a coastal sprint at dusk, where the road runs beside the sea and the light turns everything gold. You drive a small open-top car against three rivals, accelerating down straight stretches and choosing lanes around road hazards. The race is short, fast, and decided by clean driving.

The rules are simple: accelerate to gain speed, brake to slow down, and change lanes to avoid hazards. A hazard hit at speed stops the car and adds a time penalty, while a clean run finishes in ten ticks and beats every rival. The demo plays a perfect run with no crashes at all.

Speed is only useful on open road. The fastest drivers accelerate hard on the straights, pick their lane early before each hazard, and never swerve at the last second. A single crash costs more time than a cautious lane change ever will, so the speedway rewards drivers who look ahead.
controls: Type accel/brake/left/right each tick to race, quit to stop.

title: Gem Drop Cascade
description: Gem Drop Cascade is an original falling-piece puzzle about gems tumbling into a jeweler's tray. Ruby, sapphire, topaz, and emerald pieces fall one at a time, and the player slides, rotates, and drops them into the tray. When every column of the tray holds a gem at the same level, a row clears and the gems vanish in a shower of points.
body:
Gem Drop Cascade is an original falling-piece puzzle about gems tumbling into a jeweler's tray. Ruby, sapphire, topaz, and emerald pieces fall one at a time, and the player slides, rotates, and drops them into the tray. When every column of the tray holds a gem at the same level, a row clears and the gems vanish in a shower of points.

The rules are friendly: each piece can move left or right, rotate between flat and vertical, and drop into place. A flat piece fills two neighboring columns, while a vertical piece stacks two gems in one column. Clearing rows scores one hundred points each plus a small bonus per piece, and the game continues until the pieces run out.

The tray rewards flat thinking. Keep the columns level, fill the lowest gaps first, and avoid building a tall tower on one side while the other side stays empty. Players who planned one piece ahead cleared rows steadily; players who dropped pieces wherever they landed filled the tray with holes.
controls: Type left/right/rotate/drop for each falling piece, quit to stop.

title: Sharpshooter Alley
description: Sharpshooter Alley is an original gallery game about a traveling fairground shooting stall. Paper targets pop up across the back wall of the stall, each worth a different number of points, and the player has one shot at each before it folds away. The stall keeper rings a bell for every clean hit and groans theatrically at every miss.
body:
Sharpshooter Alley is an original gallery game about a traveling fairground shooting stall. Paper targets pop up across the back wall of the stall, each worth a different number of points, and the player has one shot at each before it folds away. The stall keeper rings a bell for every clean hit and groans theatrically at every miss.

The rules are simple: each round a target sits somewhere on a ten-by-ten grid, and you answer with a shot coordinate. A shot that lands on the target or one step away counts as a hit, which forgives a slightly unsteady hand. The demo plays six rounds with five hits and one clean miss.

Alley shooting rewards aiming at the target's center and taking the valuable targets first. A shot one step off still scores, so there is no reason to rush a wild guess when a careful aim will do. The best stall players looked slow because they were already aimed before the target appeared.
controls: Type shoot X Y to fire at each target, quit to stop.

demo.code:
import sys
PARAMS = {'targets': [[2, 2, 100], [5, 4, 150], [8, 8, 100], [4, 6, 200], [7, 1, 150], [1, 9, 50]]}
AUTO = ['shoot 2 2', 'shoot 5 4', 'shoot 8 7', 'shoot 4 6', 'shoot 0 0', 'shoot 1 9']

def auto_play():
    score, hits = 0, 0
    print("Gallery tribute: auto session")
    for i, target in enumerate(PARAMS["targets"]):
        shot = AUTO[i] if i < len(AUTO) else "shoot 0 0"
        parts = shot.split()
        sx, sy = int(parts[1]), int(parts[2])
        tx, ty, pts = target
        hit = abs(sx - tx) <= 1 and abs(sy - ty) <= 1
        if hit:
            score += pts
            hits += 1
        print("Round %d: target %s shot (%d,%d) %s score %d" % (i + 1, (tx, ty), sx, sy, "HIT" if hit else "MISS", score))
    print("FINAL SCORE: %d" % score)
    print("RESULT: HITS %d/%d" % (hits, len(PARAMS["targets"])))

def play():
    score, hits = 0, 0
    print("Gallery tribute: type 'shoot X Y' each round, or quit. Targets are on a 0-9 grid.")
    for i, target in enumerate(PARAMS["targets"]):
        print("Round %d: a target has appeared somewhere on the 0-9 grid." % (i + 1))
        got = False
        for line in sys.stdin:
            cmd = line.strip().lower()
            if cmd == "quit":
                print("FINAL SCORE: %d" % score)
                print("RESULT: HITS %d/%d" % (hits, len(PARAMS["targets"])))
                return
            parts = cmd.split()
            if len(parts) != 3 or parts[0] != "shoot":
                print("Use: shoot X Y")
                continue
            try:
                sx, sy = int(parts[1]), int(parts[2])
            except ValueError:
                print("Use numbers: shoot X Y")
                continue
            tx, ty, pts = target
            hit = abs(sx - tx) <= 1 and abs(sy - ty) <= 1
            if hit:
                score += pts
                hits += 1
            print("%s score %d" % ("HIT" if hit else "MISS", score))
            got = True
            break
        if not got:
            break
    print("FINAL SCORE: %d" % score)
    print("RESULT: HITS %d/%d" % (hits, len(PARAMS["targets"])))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if "--play" in sys.argv:
        play()
    else:
        auto_play()

title: Hoop Heroes Cabinet
description: Hoop Heroes Cabinet is an original basketball shooting game about a street-ball contest under festival lights. Hoop Heroes Cabinet is an original basketball shooting game about a street-ball contest under festival lights. The hoop glides along its rail to a new spot each turn, and the player must aim and shoot before the moment passes. Every basket scores two points, and a perfect run of ten baskets is the stuff of playground legend.

The rules are direct: each turn you aim at a position from zero to nine and then shoot. The hoop moves by a steady pattern from turn to turn, so a player who watches the first few hoops can predict the rest. The demo plays a perfect run, hitting all ten shots by reading the pattern.

Pattern memory is the whole game. Note where the hoop sits on the first three turns, work out the step it takes each time, and aim ahead of it rather than at where it was. Players who guessed never beat players who counted, and the contest always belonged to the counter.

title: Neon Beat Steps
description: Neon Beat Steps is an original rhythm game about dancing on a glowing floor that lights up with each beat. Arrows flash in a twelve-beat chart, and the player presses the matching key as each beat lands. Matching beats in a row builds a combo that multiplies the score, while a single miss resets the combo to zero.
body:
Neon Beat Steps is an original rhythm game about dancing on a glowing floor that lights up with each beat. Arrows flash in a twelve-beat chart, and the player presses the matching key as each beat lands. Matching beats in a row builds a combo that multiplies the score, while a single miss resets the combo to zero.

The rules are musical: each beat asks for one of four keys, left, up, down, or right, and pressing the right key scores one hundred points plus a combo bonus. The demo plays the full chart with eleven hits and one miss, showing how a combo climbs, breaks, and climbs again.

Rhythm players read one beat ahead. Watch the next arrow while you hit the current one, keep your hands relaxed, and treat a miss as a reset, not a disaster. The dancers who stayed loose kept their combos alive through the hardest stretches of the chart.
controls: Type left/up/down/right on each beat, quit to stop.

demo.code:
import sys
PARAMS = {'chart': ['left', 'left', 'up', 'right', 'down', 'up', 'left', 'right', 'down', 'down', 'up', 'right']}
AUTO = ['left', 'left', 'up', 'right', 'down', 'up', 'left', 'left', 'down', 'down', 'up', 'right']

def auto_play():
    score, combo, maxcombo, hits = 0, 0, 0, 0
    print("Rhythm tribute: auto session")
    for i, key in enumerate(PARAMS["chart"]):
        pressed = AUTO[i] if i < len(AUTO) else "miss"
        hit = (pressed == key)
        if hit:
            combo += 1
            maxcombo = max(maxcombo, combo)
            score += 100 + combo * 10
            hits += 1
        else:
            combo = 0
        print("Beat %d: need %s pressed %s %s score %d" % (i + 1, key, pressed, "HIT" if hit else "MISS", score))
    print("FINAL SCORE: %d" % score)
    print("RESULT: HITS %d/%d MAX COMBO %d" % (hits, len(PARAMS["chart"]), maxcombo))

def play():
    score, combo, maxcombo, hits = 0, 0, 0, 0
    print("Rhythm tribute: type the key for each beat (left/up/down/right), or quit.")
    for i, key in enumerate(PARAMS["chart"]):
        print("Beat %d: press a key." % (i + 1))
        pressed = None
        for line in sys.stdin:
            cmd = line.strip().lower()
            if cmd == "quit":
                print("FINAL SCORE: %d" % score)
                print("RESULT: HITS %d/%d MAX COMBO %d" % (hits, len(PARAMS["chart"]), maxcombo))
                return
            pressed = cmd
            break
        hit = (pressed == key)
        if hit:
            combo += 1
            maxcombo = max(maxcombo, combo)
            score += 100 + combo * 10
            hits += 1
        else:
            combo = 0
        print("%s score %d" % ("HIT" if hit else "MISS", score))
    print("FINAL SCORE: %d" % score)
    print("RESULT: HITS %d/%d MAX COMBO %d" % (hits, len(PARAMS["chart"]), maxcombo))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if "--play" in sys.argv:
        play()
    else:
        auto_play()

title: Ember Dungeon Quest
description: Ember Dungeon Quest is an original dungeon game about a lone adventurer carrying a single ember through dark stone rooms. Ember Dungeon Quest is an original dungeon game about a lone adventurer carrying a single ember through dark stone rooms. The dungeon holds one guardian monster, one treasure chest, and one exit door, and the ember's light is the only thing that keeps the dark back. The adventurer must defeat the guardian, claim the treasure, and reach the exit with health to spare.

The rules are clear: move through the rooms, attack a monster standing next to you, and step onto treasure to claim it. Each attack hurts the monster, but a monster that survives the blow strikes back, so a strong guardian needs two attacks and costs some health. The demo plays a full quest: two attacks, the treasure, and the exit.

Quest order matters: fight first, loot second, leave last. An adventurer who grabs the treasure first still has to pass the guardian to escape, while one who clears the guardian first walks the rest of the dungeon freely. Keep your health high before the exit, and never fight with no room to retreat.
controls: Type up/down/left/right/attack to explore, quit to stop.

title: Skyhawk Squadron
description: Skyhawk Squadron is an original scrolling shooter about a lone hawk-shaped flyer patrolling a canyon sky. Enemy flyers appear on a fixed schedule, drifting in from the right while the hawk holds its ground and picks them off. The canyon rewards patience: the hawk that waits on the right row and fires at the right moment never has to dodge at all.
body:
Skyhawk Squadron is an original scrolling shooter about a lone hawk-shaped flyer patrolling a canyon sky. Enemy flyers appear on a fixed schedule, drifting in from the right while the hawk holds its ground and picks them off. The canyon rewards patience: the hawk that waits on the right row and fires at the right moment never has to dodge at all.

The rules are steady: each tick you move up, down, left, right, or shoot, and a shot destroys an enemy on your row within four steps ahead of you. Enemies drift one step left per tick, and any enemy that reaches your position costs a life. The demo plays a twenty-one tick patrol with three kills and no lives lost.

Skyhawk pilots hold their row and let the enemy come to them. Move to the incoming enemy's row early, fire when it is close enough to hit, and never chase a flyer down the canyon. The pilots who lasted longest fired rarely and hit almost every time.
controls: Type up/down/left/right/shoot each tick to survive, quit to stop.

title: Arcade Hall Nights
description: Arcade Hall Nights is an original maze game about closing time in a friendly arcade hall. You are the night attendant walking the lanes between cabinet rows, collecting the last glowing tokens of the evening while a playful cat prowls the far lanes. The hall is quiet, the cabinets hum softly, and the cat always seems to know which lane you are heading for.
body:
Arcade Hall Nights is an original maze game about closing time in a friendly arcade hall. You are the night attendant walking the lanes between cabinet rows, collecting the last glowing tokens of the evening while a playful cat prowls the far lanes. The hall is quiet, the cabinets hum softly, and the cat always seems to know which lane you are heading for.

The rules are gentle: move through the lanes, collect every glow you step on for ten points each, and avoid the cat, who costs a life and sends you back to the entrance if you meet. You have three lives, and the night ends when the glows are gone or the lives run out.

Night attendants walk the near lanes first and save the far corner for last, when the cat's patrol is easy to predict. Never enter a dead-end lane while the cat is near, and always keep a second exit open. The maze rewards a calm, planned walk far more than a hurried dash.
controls: Type up/down/left/right to move, quit to stop.

title: Champion's Scoreboard
description: Champion's Scoreboard is an original shooting contest about a season-long festival championship. Twelve turns, one gliding hoop, and a scoreboard that records every basket: the contest is a test of steadiness across a long run rather than a single hot streak. The champion is the player whose aim holds up when the contest gets long.
body:
Champion's Scoreboard is an original shooting contest about a season-long festival championship. Twelve turns, one gliding hoop, and a scoreboard that records every basket: the contest is a test of steadiness across a long run rather than a single hot streak. The champion is the player whose aim holds up when the contest gets long.

The rules are the same as the street-ball contest: aim, then shoot, with the hoop moving by a steady pattern each turn. The demo plays twelve turns with eleven baskets and a single miss in the middle of the run, showing how a champion recovers from a miss without losing the rhythm.

Long contests reward routine over excitement. Aim the same way every turn, trust the pattern you worked out early, and treat a miss as one turn among twelve. The scoreboard belongs to the player who is still careful on the twelfth shot, not the one who was brilliant on the first.
controls: Type aim N then shoot for each turn, quit to stop.

title: Block Fusion Lab
description: Block Fusion Lab is an original falling-piece puzzle about a laboratory where energy blocks fuse in a test tray. Bolt, gear, star, and moon blocks fall one at a time, and the researcher slides, rotates, and drops them into the tray. When every column of the tray holds blocks at the same level, a row fuses and clears in a flash of light.
body:
Block Fusion Lab is an original falling-piece puzzle about a laboratory where energy blocks fuse in a test tray. Bolt, gear, star, and moon blocks fall one at a time, and the researcher slides, rotates, and drops them into the tray. When every column of the tray holds blocks at the same level, a row fuses and clears in a flash of light.

The rules are laboratory-clean: each block can move left or right, rotate between flat and vertical, and drop into place. A flat block fills two neighboring columns, while a vertical block stacks two in one column. Cleared rows score one hundred points each plus a small bonus per block, and the experiment runs for eight blocks.

The lab rewards flat trays and forward thinking. Keep the columns level, fill the lowest gaps first, and think one block ahead, because a block that looks useless now may complete the row the next block sets up. Researchers who planned ahead fused twice as many rows as those who only reacted.
controls: Type left/right/rotate/drop for each falling piece, quit to stop.
